findings.claim: 12-mark evaluation mark scheme headed '[12 marks + 3 spelling/grammar ...]'.
findings.truth: In the study-of-religions paper the SPaG marks are awarded on the 12-mark questions in the beliefs section. A practices 12-mark question carries no SPaG marks. Six SPaG marks divide as three per religion, on the beliefs question only.
findings.evidence: spec 4.4.1 assessment structure, and spec 2.2 (96 marks plus 6 SPaG)

findings.claim: 'Explain two ways in which the Lord's Prayer is used in Christian worship' is typed '4 marks — Explain Similarities & Differences'.
findings.truth: It is a 'two ways' question, so the type is '4 marks — Explain Influence'. The label picks the technique guide the student opens, so the label sent them to the wrong guide.
findings.evidence: js/main.js guide map lines 306-312; the five other 4-mark questions in this unit that do compare traditions all say 'similar or different' in the stem

findings.claim: 12-mark evaluation mark scheme headed '[12 marks + 3 spelling/grammar ...]'.
findings.truth: Same as F1: no SPaG marks on a practices 12-mark question.

findings.claim: 'Receiving Communion is considered essential for salvation.'
findings.truth: Catholic teaching makes baptism necessary for salvation. The Eucharist is the source and summit of Christian life and a source of grace, and Catholics must receive it at least once a year, but salvation is not conditional on it. The lesson body itself says 'essential for spiritual nourishment'.
findings.evidence: Catholic doctrine on baptism and the Eucharist; the lesson's own content_html wording

findings.claim: 12-mark evaluation mark scheme headed '[12 marks + 3 spelling/grammar ...]'.
findings.truth: Same as F1: no SPaG marks on a practices 12-mark question.

findings.claim: 'Christians celebrate Christmas on 25 December (though Orthodox Christians celebrate on 7 January).'
findings.truth: Only the Orthodox churches that keep the Julian calendar (Russian, Serbian, Georgian, Jerusalem) celebrate on 7 January. Greek, Romanian, Bulgarian and Antiochian Orthodox keep 25 December. The claim is true of some Orthodox Christians, not all.

findings.claim: Flashcard answer '25 December (though Orthodox Christians celebrate on 7 January).'
'Explain two ways in which Christians celebrate Christmas in Great Britain today' is typed '4 marks — Explain Similarities & Differences'.
findings.truth: Same as F2: it is a 'two ways' question and should be typed '4 marks — Explain Influence'.

findings.claim: 12-mark evaluation mark scheme headed '[12 marks + 3 spelling/grammar ...]'.
findings.truth: Same as F1: no SPaG marks on a practices 12-mark question.

findings.claim: Street Pastors 'now operates in over 300 locations across the UK'.
findings.truth: Street Pastors run in about 250 towns and cities in the UK, with around 8,000 volunteers. Founder, place and year in the same paragraph (Les Isaac, London, 2003) are correct.

findings.claim: 'Christian Aid works with communities of all faiths and none in around 37 countries.'
findings.truth: Christian Aid works in about 24 countries. 37 was its figure before it cut its country programmes.

findings.claim: Matching option 'Works with communities of all faiths in around 37 countries'.

The 1-mark 'Give/Name' question asks for two items and awards a single mark: 'Name two types of prayer used by Christians' with '[1 mark for two correct answers]'. Lessons 2 and 3 do the same (two baptism differences, two Holy Week events); lesson 4 asks for one item.
findings.truth: The paper's first four questions carry 1, 1, 4 and 6 marks, so a 1-mark question should ask for one item; asking for two and paying one mark trains a wrong habit. Two rulings are possible: (a) reword the three stems to ask for one item and pay one mark, which matches lesson 4 and the mark tariff; (b) leave them, on the view that they are recall drills rather than exam replicas. The same split runs across the whole religious-studies fleet (both 'Name two...' and 'Give one...' stems sit under the 1-mark type), so the ruling should be applied fleet-wide, not in this unit alone.
findings.evidence: spec 4.4.1 (marks 1, 1, 4, 6 and 12; AO1 tested in the first four questions); survey of 1-mark stems across the ten religious-studies units in scripts/_retrofc/units
findings.ruling: Leave: two-item 1-mark stems are a fleet-wide RS relabel item.

findings.claim: Easter 'celebrates the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, three days after his crucifixion'.
findings.truth: The credal and biblical wording is 'on the third day'. Good Friday to Easter Sunday is two days later. The glossary entry in the same lesson already says 'on the third day'. Not worth an edit: no examiner would penalise it.
findings.evidence: 1 Corinthians 15:4; the lesson's own glossary entry

findings.claim: The Lord's Prayer 'is said at worship, baptisms, marriages and funerals, uniting all Christian denominations'.
findings.truth: Quakers hold silent worship with no set prayers, and the same lesson says so. 'Nearly all' would be safer than 'all'. Too small to edit.

findings.claim: 'The Trussell Trust ... runs over 1,400 food bank centres across the UK.'
findings.truth: Still true but understated: the network reported 1,711 food bank centres in 2024-25. Also, the centres are run by local churches and charities in the network rather than by the trust itself. No edit needed.

summary: Scripture is sound: all eighteen quoted verses match the NIV in wording and reference, and the named case studies (Lourdes 1858, Bernadette, 18 visions, 72 recognised cures; Iona 563 CE, Columba; Les Isaac 2003) check out. The repeated fault is exam framing: every 12-mark practices question claims 3 SPaG marks that the paper awards in the beliefs section instead, and two 'two ways' questions carry the similarities-and-differences type, so they open the wrong technique guide. Three charity or organisation figures are out of date or overstated, one blanket claim about Orthodox Christmas needs qualifying, and one model answer overstates Catholic teaching on the Eucharist.
